To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1. We propose a novel approach to document classification by using a multimodal deep network that combines text and image information; 2. We show that the proposed method improves document classification accuracy, even when text information is noisy;
(1) the combination of text and image information improves classification accuracy; and (2) our approach is robust to OCR noise and can achieve high performance even with low quality OCR.

(a) we show that deep learning can be applied for document classification; (b) our proposed multimodal deep learning approach is able to learn text features and image features from the document images and (c) the proposed method is effective in classifying document images.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: (i) how can we design multimodal deep networks to learn from text and image for document classification, (ii) how can we use text and image to classify document images in real world setting.
the following questions: (1) What is the most efficient way to combine text and image information to classify documents? (2) What is the best way to extract text from document images?
the following questions: 1) What is the best way to learn the representation of text and image?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the multimodal approach is the best solution for document classification, and that the QS OCR text dataset is an essential resource to improve the state of the art.
our proposed approach is the first to achieve a state of the art result in the domain of document classification, and that it is the first to use multimodal learning for this task.
our multimodal deep learning architecture outperforms all the state-of-the-art methods in terms of accuracy, precision, recall and F1-score.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
our approach can learn to combine the text and the image in a single network.

we are able to classify documents based solely on the image and text information, without any other external information, with 97.2% accuracy on the Tobacco3482 dataset and 93.6% accuracy on RVL CDIP.
our proposed multimodal network outperforms the state-of-the-art on Tobacco3482, RVL CDIP and our QS OCR text dataset.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combination of image and text can be used to achieve state of the art results for document classification.
the combination of image and text information is crucial for fine grained document classification.
the multimodal neural network is able to leverage both visual and text information to achieve state of the art accuracy.
